t.1.144.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Slaying many herds of deer, those heroes, the great chariot-warriors, went away in haste, O king, passing from forest to forest.
t.1.144.2: Passing through the lands of the Matsyas, the Trigartas, the Pāñcālas and the Kīcakas, they went on, gazing at lovely stretches of forest and at lakes.
t.1.144.4: Sometimes carrying their mother, the great chariot-warriors hurried along; sometimes moving at their own pleasure, they then went on again swiftly.
t.1.144.3: All of them, having twisted their own hair into matted locks and clad in bark garments and deerskins, the great-souled ones, together with Kuntī, bore the appearance of ascetics.
t.1.144.5: Studying the sacred Veda and all the Vedāṅgas in their entirety, as well as the science of polity, those knowers of dharma saw their grandfather.
t.1.144.6: Then, having saluted the great-souled Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, all those scorchers of foes stood with their mother, their palms joined in reverence.
t.1.144.7: O bulls among the Bharatas, I knew this beforehand in my mind: how you were driven into exile by the Dhārtarāṣṭras, who stand firm in adharma.
t.1.144.8: Knowing that, I have come, wishing to do you the highest good. You should not despair over this; all this is for your happiness.
t.1.144.10: Therefore my affection for you is now all the greater; out of affection I wish to do what is good for you. Hear that from me.
t.1.144.11: This town nearby is delightful and free from sickness; dwell here in disguise, awaiting my return.
t.1.144.9: All of them stand equal in my regard, and so do you, there is no doubt; yet kinsmen show greater affection to one who is in distress and to one who is young.
t.1.144.12: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted those Pārthas, tamers of their foes, the lordly Vyāsa went to Ekacakrā and consoled Kuntī.
t.1.144.13: O mother of living sons, this son of yours, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, a king of righteousness, will rule over all the kings on the earth.
t.1.144.14: Having conquered the whole earth by dharma, this self-controlled knower of dharma will, without doubt, enjoy it through the might of Bhīmasena and Arjuna.
t.1.144.15: Your sons and Mādrī's, all of them great chariot-warriors, will then roam happily and with glad hearts in their own kingdom.
t.1.144.16: And these tigers among men, having conquered this earth, will sacrifice with the Rājasūya, the Aśvamedha and other rites abounding in sacrificial gifts.
t.1.144.17: Favoring their circle of friends with wealth and with happiness, your sons will enjoy here the kingdom of their fathers and grandfathers.
t.1.144.18: Having spoken thus and settled them in the dwelling of a brahmin, the seer Dvaipāyana then addressed the best of kings.
t.1.144.20: Answered "So be it" by all of them with joined palms, O lord of men, the blessed Vyāsa, the mighty seer, departed as he wished.
t.1.144.19: Wait for me here; I shall come again. Only once you have understood the right place and time will you know supreme joy.
